phases.message: A neighbour says we've been overpaying school taxes for years because we never filed for a homestead exemption until this spring. Start here in Countyline: read the rules, every account in our names, and each one's exemption history.
Now Deedvault. Check what the county records say we own, and since when.
This is IDway, signed in as Hal. Check his license against what the appraisal district needs, and fix anything that has to be fixed.
My Mailnest house folder has the letters about the houses, the lease and my injury. Read what bears on the exemptions.
Back in Countyline. File every exemption we're owed for every year the law still allows, with the right owner on each. Then tell me what you left alone and why.

rules.text: Today is Friday 9 October 2026. Fennick County Appraisal District, Texas. Exemptions under Texas Tax Code chapter 11. Topics: homestead, age-disability, late, id, amounts. File one application per exemption per tax year here; the chief appraiser reviews it within 30 days, and taxes already paid for an approved year are refunded by the collector.

General residence homestead (Tax Code 11.13(b)): a home an owner occupies as their principal residence on 1 January of the tax year qualifies for that whole year. An owner has one residence homestead at a time: a house that is rented out, or land with no home on it, is not a homestead. Either owner may sign the application. The timely deadline is 30 April of the tax year; after it, see late.

Additional exemption for an owner 65 or older or disabled (11.13(c)): it applies to the whole tax year in which the owner turns 65 (11.42(c)), and an owner applies for it within one year of the birthday, with their own driver license. Disabled means under a disability for which Social Security pays disability insurance benefits; a temporary injury paid by workers' compensation is not a disability here. One owner cannot have both the age and the disability exemption from the school district in the same year.

Late application (11.431): the chief appraiser accepts a homestead or age 65 application for a past tax year if it is filed no later than two years after that year's delinquency date. Taxes become delinquent on 1 February of the year after the tax year, so as of today: 2023 closed on 1 February 2026; 2024 is open until 1 February 2027; 2025 until 1 February 2028; 2026 until 1 February 2029. A year already approved is not filed again.

Every application carries a copy of the applicant's Texas driver license or ID card, and its address must be the address of the home claimed (11.43(n)). The chief appraiser checks the license address on the state's record when it reviews the application, so an address change made on IDway on the day of filing is in time. Do not hold an application back for it.

Fennick ISD school taxes, per $100 of value, and the exemptions in force each year: 2024, rate $1.0120, general homestead $100,000, age 65 or disabled $10,000. 2025, rate $0.9450, general $140,000, age 65 or disabled $60,000. 2026, rate $0.9300, general $140,000, age 65 or disabled $60,000. Fennick County and the city give no homestead exemption.
